text:
sylvie: Heads-up — nightly perf dashboard just alerted on a sudden p95 tail jump for short-text generates (median ~90ms -> p95 ~220ms) starting ~00:20 UTC. See chart: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/nightly/kernel-selection

matt: I saw the same when I checked the canary CI run. Kernel selector acceptance rate flipped to fallback path much more often. Failing metric is kernel_switch_latency and overall request duration.

jas: Did a quick bisect on the canary branch — suspecting PR 4321 (batching heuristic overhaul + new prefetch logic). Bisect points to commit abc1234 that introduced "opportunistic_stride".

carla: Can we pin the rollout or revert? This is hitting nightly jobs and a small subset of production canaries.

infra-bot: deploy:canary reported rollout 4321 -> failed health checks in region us-west-2 at 00:18 UTC. Autoscaler retried 2/3.

matt: Reproduced locally with a synthetic short request load. Profiling shows KV cache miss rate jumped ~3x for seq_len=16. Looks like batch stride expanded and caused more KV key churn/evictions.

sylvie: Pasted short flame output from perf profiler — eviction hot loop dominant after commit abc1234:
```
Hot functions:
  kv_cache::evict_if_needed  37.2%
  batcher::add_request       22.8%
  kernel_selector::score     15.4%
  allocator::compact         9.1%
```
KV evictions per second went from ~120 -> ~410 under the same qps.

jas: That matches my hypothesis — opportunistic_stride increases batch size/stride to favor throughput but doesn't respect KV locality. For short requests we lose cache locality and thrash.

carla: Suggest immediate mitigation: rollback opportunistic_stride to previous default and lower batch window to 5ms in canary. That should reduce batch coalescing and preserve KV locality.

matt: I opened PR 4377 with two quick fixes: revert the stride change and add a runtime flag `runtime.disable_opportunistic_stride=true` + `batch.window_ms=5` for canary. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4377

ops-qa: Can we add a short-term alert to watch p95 delta > 50ms for short requests and also track KV eviction_rate? I'll add a dashboard panel and pager if it persists after rollout.

infra-bot: CI:perf-smoke job queued for PR 4377, run 422. Expected ~10m.

jas: I ran a local patched build with the revert flag — perf looks back to baseline for seq_len 8/16 tests. KV evictions dropped to ~130/s. Will monitor canary once merged.

sylvie: Added triage notes to the incident doc and playbook: steps to toggle `disable_opportunistic_stride`, reduce batch window, and how to collect kv_counters and kernel_selector samples.

carla: Approving quick revert; merging PR 4377 to canary now. Will hold full rollout until two green nightly cycles.

matt: After merge, CI perf-smoke passed. Nightly pipeline is green for the next run at 01:00 UTC. I'll keep an eye on the dashboard and post updates.

ops-qa: Watching dashboard. If p95 spike reappears, escalate to oncall. Added runbook snippet: check commit range, toggle runtime flag, and gather `perf flame` and `kv_histogram` (example queries included).

sylvie: Thanks everyone — big win catching this before full rollout. Leaving the thread open for any regressions over the next 24h.

matt: noted — logging a follow-up PR to make opportunistic stride opt-in behind a workload profile instead of default on.

jas: +1, will pair on the follow-up.

infra-bot: alert resolved: nightly p95 delta returned to baseline at 01:12 UTC.
